precepts.text: Two: at Marah. The waters were bitter, and the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?
precepts.point: Because all those men which have seen my glory and my miracles have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice. Write the ten down; the Most High deals in numbers, and nothing in the Bible is insignificant.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Number two of the ten times the children of Israel tempted the Lord is at Marah, m-a-r-a-h. Write it down so you are not confused if it comes up again.

“And when they came to Marah, they could not drink of the waters of Marah, for they were bitter: therefore the name of it was called Marah. And the people murmured against Moses, saying, What shall we drink?”

The people complained because the water was bitter. They had just seen the Lord overthrow the Egyptians in the midst of the sea, and at the first bitter water they murmured against Moses. That is the provoking the Lord speaks of in Numbers 14:22: men “which have seen my glory, and my miracles”, and still did not hearken to his voice.

precepts.text: Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. While all things were in quiet silence, thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war. The word of God, the anointed Christ, has a throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he came down for war; he leaped off his throne. That is why Moses says the Lord God is a man of war. He brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death. A lot of you did not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of the enemies of Israel. And the Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams, so they should not perish without knowing why they were afflicted.
precepts.point: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy. This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: when the Lord fought against the Egyptians, drowned them in the Red Sea, and brought plagues upon them.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Some people still question it and say the Lord in Exodus 15:3 is the Father. Solomon gave the same account Moses gave. “For while all things were in quiet silence, and that night was in the midst of her swift course, Thine Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction”.

Who is the word of God? The anointed, Christ. He has a royal throne in the heavens, and during Exodus he leaped off his throne and came down for war. So when Moses says “The Lord is a man of war”, he is speaking of the word of God that came down at the Passover, killed the Egyptians and drowned them in the Red Sea. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring for his people.

He “brought thine unfeigned commandment as a sharp sword, and standing up filled all things with death; and it touched the heaven, but it stood upon the earth.” The Lord filled all things with death when he came down in Exodus. A lot of you do not fully understand what Passover is really about: it is about death and destruction of our enemies.

“Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them sore, and terrors came upon them unlooked for. And one thrown here, and another there, half dead, shewed the cause of his death. For the dreams that troubled them did foreshew this, lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.” The Lord sent the Egyptians horrible visions and dreams; he was afflicting them and warring with them. That is the right hand of Exodus 15:6 that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy.”

precepts.text: The second man is the Lord from heaven. The Lord from heaven is Christ: that is the Almighty word that leaped off his throne and came down in Exodus.
precepts.point: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. Thy right hand, O Lord, hath dashed in pieces the enemy. This is the wars of the Lord we are reading about: when the Lord fought against the Egyptians, drowned them in the Red Sea, and brought plagues upon them.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

precepts.why:
Who is the Almighty word that leaped down off his throne? “The first man is of the earth, earthy: the second man is the Lord from heaven.” The Lord from heaven is Christ. He is the one who came down and killed the Egyptians in Exodus, and that is why Moses says the Lord is a man of war.

Paul says the same thing about the wilderness: our fathers “drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ.” And Exodus 13:21: “the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire”. That pillar of cloud was a chariot, and the Lord inside it was Christ. Who was following us in the wilderness? Christ. Who killed the Egyptians? Christ.

So when Exodus 15:3 says “the Lord is his name”, it is speaking of the anointed. He smote the Egyptians, and the same way he is going to come back in the future and smite spiritual Egypt, the land we are living in today.

precepts.text: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help and trust in chariots but look not to the Holy One of Israel: all Egypt's power did not save it, he will not call back his word, and evil is set for all these nations while you sit in confederacy with them thinking all nations are saved.
precepts.point: The Most High loves his people, and as the wars come, hard times are coming for the twelve tribes.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
The Lord is a man of war, and his vengeance is on all the nations read in Psalms 83; he has a big payback coming for all of them. Egypt is one example. Exodus 15 says “Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea”, and Isaiah 31 shows what all that power was worth: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help; and stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong”.

Did the power help them? No. All their chariots and all their war materials did not help them at all. And “they look not unto the Holy One of Israel, neither seek the Lord!” We did not look to the Holy One of Israel, to our God, to save us. The God of Israel is the only God that is going to save us out of all this foolishness. The wars are going to come to the point where thermonuclear ICBMs are put in full effect and a lot of people die, and the question to ask yourself is, will it be us?

“Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil, and will not call back his words”. He is not calling back his word. Evil is set for all these nations, and these nations will be destroyed. Where will you be? You cannot have God to trust in and Christ coming to save you while you sit in confederacy with all these nations, thinking all nations are going to be saved and we are all together. That is not the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

So the right hand that “hath dashed in pieces the enemy” in Exodus 15:6 is the same hand that will overthrow every nation Israel trusts in instead of him.

precepts.text: O thou that dwellest upon many waters, abundant in treasures, thine end is come: America will not step down or meet the demands, so the Lord fills her with men as with caterpillars, the wild and crazy ones.
precepts.point: The Most High loves his people, and as the wars come, hard times are coming for the twelve tribes.

note.label: The God Of War & Salvation

precepts.why:
Prophecy is coming to pass and there is no stopping it. The wild and crazy ones made demands to the proud one: not only fall back out of our country, but pay us back for all the destruction. The proud man says no, we are not going to do that. Even while they talk about peace talks, God has them in the trick bag.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: that is New Babylon, America. She is “abundant in treasures”: rich from all the nations, because they have taken all the land and all the resources and oppressed all the people. And “thine end is come, and the measure of thy covetousness.” The Most High is already telling her that her end is come and it is time to step down. She is not going to step down, so God is going to put her down.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”: the same Lord of hosts who is a man of war in Exodus 15:3. “Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers; and they shall lift up a shout against thee.” Those caterpillars are the wild and crazy ones.

If proud Babylon gives in to the demands, she loses her sovereignty over the economy, and that is her downfall. Because she is prideful and already in power, she will not do it, so it leads to war, and God activates the caterpillars. Either way it goes to war. As the Lord cast Pharaoh's chariots into the sea, he will consume this enemy as stubble.

precepts.text: My son, forget not my law, but let thine heart keep my commandments; the heart is the mind, and the laws are the commandments. Length of days, long life, and peace shall they add to thee: despite wars and mayhem, you want peace, do what he said. Trust in the Lord with all thine heart and lean not unto thine own understanding: trust that the prophecies go in order, Iran will not bring in World War III but will help unite the Arabs. The understanding is not I am already saved; it is he that endureth to the end shall be saved, and he shall direct thy paths.
precepts.point: The Lord is a man of war. We serve a terrible God who is also merciful, and he is going to use these nations to create a final battle. I pray I make it and you make it.

note.label: Wars Are Here: Seek Good Not Evil

precepts.why:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war.
precepts.point: I form the light and create darkness; I make peace and create evil; I the Lord do all these things.

note.label: War of the Gods

precepts.why:
In Isaiah 45 the Lord says, “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect, I have even called thee by thy name: I have surnamed thee, though thou hast not known me”. God surnamed us, and even though he revealed himself to us and delivered us numerous times, we kept turning our backs on him. “I am the Lord, and there is none else, there is no God beside me”. Some set themselves up as gods, and some create gods in their minds and as idols, but there is none with him. “I form the light, and create darkness: I make peace, and create evil: I the Lord do all these things”.

Exodus 15:3 fills in the picture: “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name”. The same Lord that forms the light, creates darkness, makes peace and creates evil is also a man of war. That is the overall picture of the Lord our God.

Psalms 46 shows what that looks like: “Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth”. Pharaohs were worshipped as gods, Xerxes thought he was a god, and Antiochus Epiphanes thought he was God manifest on earth; rulers rise in power and rise in pride. But “He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder”. The man on the thumbnail who has claimed for two years that he will stop the war between Ukraine and Russia has not stopped anything. When the Iron Dome in Israel failed and the rockets came through, that was no technical glitch; the Lord ripped it open. He makes the prideful instruments of man fail, because he decides where war happens and when it ceases.

And that God of war, who formed the light and created darkness, is Christ. He is our refuge, and he teaches his soldiers to do the same: “Blessed be the Lord my strength, which teacheth my hands to war, and my fingers to fight”. He handpicked us to be soldiers in his army.

precepts.text: Fear not, thou worm Jacob; I will help thee, saith the Lord and thy redeemer.
precepts.point: The Lord is a man of war. War is coming to this place, and through those wars Israel's salvation comes.

note.label: Destroyed by Familiar Hands

precepts.why:
The Bible says God is a man of war. War is coming to this place; God is bringing war to the earth. And we should not be afraid of it. Isaiah 41: “For I the Lord thy God will hold thy right hand, saying unto thee, Fear not; I will help thee. Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee, saith the Lord, and thy redeemer, the Holy One of Israel”. God is talking to us. Don't be afraid; he is going to help us.

Read on: “Behold, I will make thee a new sharp threshing instrument having teeth: thou shalt thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and shalt make the hills as chaff”. A new sharp threshing instrument is a weapon, a weapon of war. The mountains are the nations, and we are going to beat them small. “Thou shalt fan them, and the wind shall carry them away, and the whirlwind shall scatter them”. A time is coming when we will say, there was a place named America; what happened to it? It will be wiped out and never remembered again.

So when war comes, we should be celebrating, happy, not sad, because through those wars our salvation and our freedom come. We should pray for that thing. Our job now is to prepare for it, spiritually and mentally, not physically: prepare ourselves and our people, and keep a food pantry, as Bishop has been teaching for a while.

That preparing is spiritual warfare: “For though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh”; the weapons of our warfare are “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Don't get caught up in the foolishness of this place, the marches and the stupidity, even with your own family. Stay in the scripture, cast down every evil imagination in the minds of our people, and bring every thought “to the obedience of Christ”, the black Messiah. The man of war fights for us.

precepts.text: The Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle; He is a man of war.
precepts.point: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is His name. He loves war against His enemies; our carnal minds cannot fathom it, but the word says what it says. He mustereth the host of the battle: He brought the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks, and the Romans against Israel, and He has stood in the midst of the wars of the nations ever since.

note.label: Exodus 15: The Song of Moses: The Lord Is a Man of War

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” He loves war against His enemies. Our carnal minds cannot fathom it, but the word says what it says. The song of Moses is a prophecy as well, speaking not only of the coming out of Egypt but in the future tense.

Isaiah shows the man of war at work among the nations: “The noise of a multitude in the mountains, like as of a great people; a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together: the Lord of hosts mustereth the host of the battle.” The Lord of hosts musters the host of the battle. He brought the Babylonians, the Persians and Medes, the Greeks and the Romans against Israel, and He has stood in the midst of the wars of the nations ever since.

The one who threw the horse and his rider into the sea is the one gathering the kingdoms of nations together for battle. That is His name.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war; the tribes came out as armies.
precepts.point: Moses wrote their goings out by the commandment of the Lord. The Lord gave the word, and great was the company of those that published it; so the claim that another people wrote the scriptures falls, for Moses wrote what God commanded him to write.

note.label: Exodus 19: The Covenant at Mount Sinai

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” That is why the children of Israel went forth out of Egypt with their armies. The tribes are armies, because the Lord who brought them out is a man of war.

Israel has always been at war, and Israel is at war today: a spiritual war.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: a man. The scriptures give no ground to those who say God is a woman; he deals with the men of Israel, and no woman is to usurp authority over the man.
precepts.point: Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there, so the Most High had to say plainly, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” A man. The scriptures give no ground to those who say God is a woman.

Israel had come out of Egypt, where graven images filled the land and where the likeness of the female was worshipped. Egypt is where feminism was already incorporated: Hathor the cattle goddess and Qetesh the goddess of beauty were among the idols learned there. So the Most High had to say plainly, no “likeness of male or female”, no deity male or female. There is no goddess in the scriptures.

The Lord is a man of war. He deals with the men of Israel, and no woman is to usurp authority over the man.

precepts.text: Miriam the prophetess led the women with timbrels and dances; her place was over the women, not over the body.
precepts.point: Moses said set a man over the congregation, not a woman, because women were never ordained to lead the children of Israel; that does not fit the divine order of the Most High. Miriam was a prophetess and one of the chief women, and she led the women; women have a real role in the nation, but leading the body is not it. When Miriam got puffed up and spoke against Moses, she was judged.

note.label: Joshua 1: The Charge to Joshua and the Formula for Success

precepts.why:
“And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.” Miriam was a prophetess and one of the chief women, and she led the women with timbrels and dances.

Her place was over the women, not over the body. Women have a real role in the nation, but leading the body is not it; that is why Moses said set a man over the congregation, and why the Lord named Joshua.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
precepts.point: The captain of the host of the Lord is Christ, the captain of our salvation. This is why Joshua was afraid: the return of Christ is not the soft picture Christianity paints, for he is not coming back made like unto his brethren as at the first, but with the power of the living God, to take vengeance and destroy. No missiles or fighter jets will do anything against him.

note.label: Joshua 5: Circumcision of the Flesh and of the Heart

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The one Joshua saw was a warrior, a man with his sword drawn in his hand, and he came as captain of the host of the Lord. That is who the Lord is: a man of war.

So the captain of the army of the Lord standing over against Joshua by Jericho was no soft figure. He is a man of war, and Joshua fell on his face.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name.
precepts.point: He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; the only reason they got big numbers is that they are being fattened for destruction.

note.label: Joshua 10: The Day the Sun Stood Still

precepts.why:
Joshua “utterly destroyed all that breathed, as the Lord God of Israel commanded”, and took all these kings and their land at one time, “because the Lord God of Israel fought for Israel.” This is why they tell you not to read the Old Testament: the Most High is out there fighting through his people, giving them the spirit to destroy all that breathe, both young and old, leaving none alive.

“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” That is who fought for Israel. A man of war is his name.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
precepts.point: The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Othniel “judged Israel, and went out to war”, because “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The spirit of the Lord came upon him, and a man with that spirit judges and goes to war.

That answers those who ask, when we are out on the streets teaching, where are your women. They are not at war; the Lord is a man of war. And it answers our people today who say, you can't judge me: the spirit of the Most High came upon Othniel and he judged Israel.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war, the LORD is his name; many who think they know God have no idea who they are dealing with.
precepts.point: The reason is given: that the cruelty done to the threescore and ten sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid upon Abimelech their brother, which slew them, and upon the men of Shechem, which aided him in the killing of his brethren. The hired men and the backers carried the blood guilt too. Abimelech ran for three years and everything looked good, but you are not getting away with evil.

note.label: Judges 9: Abimelech and the Fire Out of the Bramble

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name. Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red sea.”

Many who think they know God have no idea who they are dealing with. He is a man of war; that is his name. He cast Pharaoh's chariots and captains into the sea, and he sends an evil spirit between a king and the city that made him king. The strife at Shechem is the Lord at war against Abimelech for the blood of his brethren.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war; contests of strength were known among His people.
precepts.point: When Asahel refused to turn aside, Abner smote him with the hinder end of the spear under the fifth rib, and he died there. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. Those who came to the place stood still; the lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

note.label: 2 Samuel 2: David Anointed King Over Judah

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.”

At the pool of Gibeon, Abner said to Joab, “Let the young men now arise, and play before us. And Joab said, Let them arise.” To play there means to compete and battle one another. The Lord is a man of war, and contests of strength like this were known among his people and done in that day.

Twelve of Benjamin and twelve of David’s servants “caught every one his fellow by the head, and thrust his sword in his fellow’s side; so they fell down together”, and that place was called Helkath-hazzurim. Then “there was a very sore battle that day; and Abner was beaten, and the men of Israel, before the servants of David.”

Asahel, “as light of foot as a wild roe”, meaning he was fast, pursued Abner and would not turn aside, though Abner warned him again and again: “wherefore should I smite thee to the ground? how then should I hold up my face to Joab thy brother?” When he refused, Abner smote him “with the hinder end of the spear” under the fifth rib, “that the spear came out behind him”. A strong thrust is needed to drive a spear through a man, and Abner was strong. As many as came to the place stood still. The lesson is to take heed to the warning and not keep testing a man.

precepts.text: The LORD is a man of war: the LORD is his name; no war did Israel win alone.
precepts.point: The Philistines left their images there, and David and his men burned them. David knew the law, that the graven images of the nations were to be burned with fire and their silver and gold not desired, lest a man be snared and cursed by bringing an abomination into his house.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” When the Philistines came up to seek David, he did not go to war on his own strength. He enquired of the Lord, “Shall I go up to the Philistines? wilt thou deliver them into mine hand?” He knew where his power lay.

The Lord answered, “Go up: for I will doubtless deliver the Philistines into thine hand.” And when David smote them he gave the Lord the victory: “The Lord hath broken forth upon mine enemies before me, as the breach of waters.” So he called the place Baal-perazim.

The Philistines had already lost their champion Goliath, and still they came to challenge this man. But the victory was the Lord's, because the Lord is a man of war. No war did Israel win alone.

precepts.text: The Most High is a man of war and knows exactly how to handle the battle.
precepts.point: David did exactly as commanded and smote them from Gibeon to Gazer. The lesson is precise obedience: if he says do not go up, do not go up; if he says go this way, do not go that way.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 14: David Established and Inquiring of the Most High

precepts.why:
“The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The Most High is a man of war, and He knows exactly how to handle the battle.

When the Philistines came up a second time, David did not presume on the first victory; he “enquired again of God”. This time the Most High told him, “Go not up after them; turn away from them, and come upon them over against the mulberry trees.” He was to move only “when thou shalt hear a sound of going in the tops of the mulberry trees”, “for God is gone forth before thee to smite the host of the Philistines.” The man of war laid out the battle Himself and went before David.

precepts.text: Miriam the prophetess took a timbrel in her hand, and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances, showing that music is a form of prophecy.
precepts.point: The sons of Asaph prophesied according to the order of the king, the sons of Jeduthun prophesied with a harp to give thanks and to praise the Lord, and the sons of Heman were given by God to lift up the horn, for God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 25: The Singers and Musicians of the Sanctuary

precepts.why:
“And Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances.” When Miriam came out, she led the women in prophecy, and it was with music. Music is a form of prophecy.

That is why David and the captains separated the sons of Asaph, Heman and Jeduthun, “who should prophesy with harps, with psalteries, and with cymbals”. The sons of Asaph “prophesied according to the order of the king”, and Jeduthun “prophesied with a harp, to give thanks and to praise the Lord.” The sons of Heman were given by God to lift up the horn, for God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters.

precepts.text: In His mercy He led forth the people He redeemed and guided them in His strength unto His holy habitation; He is our redeemer.
precepts.point: Only in our affliction do we, many times, consider God and turn our mind and spirit back to the Most High, keeping His laws, statutes, and commandments. Once we start to go off, the Lord will touch us up any way He wants.

note.label: Psalm 78: The History of Israel's Rebellion and the Choosing of Judah and David

precepts.why:
“And they remembered that God was their rock, and the high God their redeemer.” Moses sang of that redeemer at the Red Sea: “Thou in thy mercy hast led forth the people which thou hast redeemed: thou hast guided them in thy strength unto thy holy habitation.”

In his mercy he led forth the people he redeemed and guided them in his strength unto his holy habitation. He is our redeemer. That is what our fathers remembered when he slew them and they returned and sought him early: the God who brought them out was the one they had gone off from.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

points: The history up to this point: they were serving hard bondage as slaves in Egypt. Out of nowhere the Most High brought Moses to deliver them. They saw the water turn to blood throughout the land. They seen plagues drop on the Egyptians and not them. They literally witnessed the power of God show that all them Egyptian gods was nothing and that he was the one true God. God killed the firstborn of everyone who did not have the blood on the posts of their doors. They walked up out of Egypt with gold and jewelry, everything the Egyptians that was oppressing them had. The Lord split the Red Sea for them; they walked in between two waters to safety and the Egyptians got swallowed up behind them. They seen all of this miraculous power happen, and then they got to the wilderness talking about, I'm thirsty.
How? You get to the wilderness after you done seen all this power, and now you worried about water, like the Lord don't know you need something to drink?

note.label: Jude 1:16

points: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name. When Moses says this, he is talking about something much more. Moses said it because he saw the Lord warring for his people. And this Lord is talking about Christ the anointed.

note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: Pharaoh's chariots and his host hath he cast into the sea: his chosen captains also are drowned in the Red Sea. Who did that? The Lord. note.label: The Book of the Wars of the Lord

points: The Lord is a man of war: he loves to see a sword, a shield and blood on a battlefield, an intimate war rather than long-distance shooting. Pharaoh's chariots cast into the sea are nations sacrificed on our behalf, and his right hand dashed the enemy in pieces.
